item.title: Amami Oshima Island — Guide
item.description: Amami Oshima, a large subtropical island in the seas between Kyushu and Okinawa (part of Kagoshima), is a paradise of natural beauty recognised as a UNESCO World Heritage site for its unique biodiversity. Ringed by white-sand beaches, coral reefs and clear turquoise seas ideal for swimming, snorkelling, diving and kayaking, its interior holds lush subtropical laurel forests and mangroves that are home to rare endemic species, including the elusive Amami rabbit, found nowhere else on earth.
